title: Sparse derivatives with sparsediff
text: sparsediff thin R interface SparseDiffEngine C library — sparse Jacobian Hessian differentiation backend used CVXPY Disciplined Nonlinear Programming (DNLP) extension. R analog Python sparsediffpy package wraps C library. build nonlinear expression graph sd_* atom constructors, assemble pieces problem, evaluate, primal point, objective value dense gradient, constraint vector sparse Jacobian (COO form), lower-triangular Lagrangian Hessian (COO form). low-level backend: intended user higher-level modelling layer CVXR, analyst writing models hand. walk-shows moving parts.

title: Sparse derivatives with sparsediff
text: Leaves created sd_variable() (slice differentiation vector) sd_parameter() (fixed data). Everything else atom applied expressions. constructor returns expression handle — external pointer engine’s graph frees garbage collected. f(x) = sum(exp(x)) length-3 variable, single linear constraint g(x) = sum(x): var_id 0-based, column-major offset variable’s first entry flat primal vector; n_vars total number variables. Reduction axis follows engine convention: -1 (entries), 0 (rows), 1 (across columns).
code: n   <- 3L x   <- sd_variable(d1 = n, d2 = 1L, var_id = 0L, n_vars = n)  # 0-based var offset obj <- sd_sum(sd_exp(x), axis = -1L)                          # sum(exp(x))  (axis -1 = all) g1  <- sd_sum(x, axis = -1L)                                  # sum(x)

title: Sparse derivatives with sparsediff
text: Evaluation ordered: forward pass populates node values primal point u, gradient, Jacobian values Hessian values can read. constraint Jacobian comes back COO form (0-based row/column indices) plus matching nonzero values: Lagrangian Hessian lower triangle obj_w * Hess(f) + sum_i w[] * Hess(g_i). objective weight 1 constraint linear (zero Hessian), result diag(exp(u)):
code: u <- c(0, 0.5, 1)  sd_objective_forward(prob, u)   # value of sum(exp(x)) #> [1] 5.367003 sd_gradient(prob)               # gradient = exp(u) #> [1] 1.000000 1.648721 2.718282  sd_constraint_forward(prob, u)  # value of sum(x) #> [1] 1.5 sd_jacobian_sparsity(prob)      # rows / cols / nrow / ncol #> $rows #> [1] 0 0 0 #>  #> $cols #> [1] 0 1 2 #>  #> $nrow #> [1] 1 #>  #> $ncol #> [1] 3 sd_jacobian_values(prob)        # d/dx sum(x) = (1, 1, 1) #> [1] 1 1 1 sd_hessian_sparsity(prob) #> $rows #> [1] 0 1 2 #>  #> $cols #> [1] 0 1 2 #>  #> $nrow #> [1] 3 #>  #> $ncol #> [1] 3 sd_hessian_values(prob, obj_w = 1, w = 0) #> [1] 1.000000 1.648721 2.718282

title: Sparse derivatives with sparsediff
text: sd_parameter() fixed data can updated evaluations without rebuilding graph — basis CVXPY/CVXR’s Disciplined Parametrized Programming (DPP) fast path. Register parameters , push new values sd_update_params():
code: p    <- sd_parameter(d1 = 1L, d2 = 1L, param_id = 0L, n_vars = n, values = 2) obj2 <- sd_sum(sd_scalar_mult(p, sd_exp(x)), axis = -1L)      # theta * sum(exp(x)) prob2 <- sd_problem(obj2, constraints = list(), verbose = FALSE) sd_register_params(prob2, list(p)) sd_init_derivatives(prob2)  sd_objective_forward(prob2, u)        # theta = 2 #> [1] 10.73401 sd_update_params(prob2, 3)            # theta -> 3 sd_objective_forward(prob2, u)        # re-evaluated, no rebuild #> [1] 16.10101

title: sparsediff 0.6.1
text: CRAN release: 2026-10-06 bundled SparseDiffEngine moves 0.3.0 0.6.1, release ‘sparsediffpy’ 0.6.x ‘CVXPY’ 1.9.3 use. release , package version matches bundled engine version. Fixed: parametric problem re-evaluated sd_update_params() return values computed old parameter values (engine fix #107). modeling layer meant re-solving parametric nonlinear problem changing parameter returned previous solution, reported optimal. Fixed: selecting entries repeated indices sd_index() (example quadratic objective symmetric variable) crash R bus error Jacobian Hessian evaluated (engine fix #105). New sd_quad_form_dense(): quadratic form dense constant parametric matrix. parametric form follows sd_update_params(). sd_quad_form() keeps signature still takes sparse constant matrix. Every ‘sparsediffpy’ 0.6.1 function now sd_* counterpart calls engine routine arguments; name map package help page (?sparsediff). New: sd_left_kron() sd_right_kron() (Kronecker products, used next CVXPY release), compressed-sparse-row derivative accessors sd_jacobian(), sd_get_jacobian(), sd_init_hessian(), sd_hessian() sd_get_hessian(), sd_get_expr_dimensions() / sd_get_expr_size(). sd_rel_entr() now dispatches operand size like make_rel_entr. Fixed: sd_init_hessian_coo() crashed R called Jacobian initialized; now initializes Jacobian first. sd_rel_entr(), sd_rel_entr_first_scalar() sd_rel_entr_second_scalar() now check arguments two different variables, engine requires; arguments overflowed heap buffer (found AddressSanitizer). BLAS shim gains cblas_ddot, 0.6.1 engine calls. Fixed: package failed compile Linux systems glibc 2.36 older (example Debian 12), _GNU_SOURCE defined late fopencookie(). now set compiler command line. Documentation: sparse matrix arguments sd_quad_form() sd_left_matmul() / sd_right_matmul() compressed-sparse-row arrays, dense data arguments row-major. Earlier documentation said compressed-sparse-column column-major. grouped help pages now usage sections (flagged current R-devel). package now ‘testthat’ test suite.
